project.name: sc2-helper
project.description: Real-time StarCraft II assistant that monitors the HUD via screen OCR and fires spoken warnings when resources are floating, supply is capped, or workers are idle.

nodes.name: _extract_result
nodes.summary: Looks up the Win/Loss/Tie result for a specific player from the SC2 API players list, falling back to any player's result if the indexed lookup fails.

nodes.name: _extract_race
nodes.summary: Normalizes the player's race string (e.g., 'Prot' → 'Protoss') from the SC2 API players list.

nodes.name: _format_debug_state
nodes.summary: Formats a game state dict into a human-readable debug string showing minerals, gas, supply, and idle workers.

nodes.name: hud_elements.py
nodes.summary: Defines the HudElement frozen dataclass and the canonical HUD_ELEMENTS list used to identify which screen regions to OCR for minerals, gas, supply, and idle workers.

nodes.name: HudElement
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass representing a single SC2 HUD element with its key, display label, and default OCR capture region size.

nodes.name: messages.py
nodes.summary: Stores all spoken warning message banks (strict, funny variants for supply, minerals, gas, idle workers) and the get_message() dispatcher that selects messages by mode.

nodes.name: get_message
nodes.summary: Selects and returns a warning message string for a given category and mode (strict, funny, or custom), falling back gracefully when custom messages are missing.

nodes.name: ocr.py
nodes.summary: Provides screen capture via mss and Tesseract OCR functions for reading integer HUD values and the supply fraction (used/max) from captured screen regions.

nodes.name: capture_region
nodes.summary: Captures a rectangular screen region using mss and returns it as a PIL Image.

nodes.name: ocr_number
nodes.summary: Runs Tesseract OCR on a preprocessed HUD region image to extract a single integer, returning None on parse failure.

nodes.name: ocr_supply
nodes.summary: Runs Tesseract OCR on the supply HUD region to extract a 'used/max' tuple, logging a warning and returning (None, None) on failure.

nodes.name: find_coords.py
nodes.summary: Standalone macOS calibration script that prompts the user to hover over each SC2 HUD element and records the mouse coordinates using Quartz, then prints the region config values.

nodes.name: get_mouse_pos
nodes.summary: Returns the current macOS mouse cursor position as (x, y) integers using the Quartz CoreGraphics API.

nodes.name: detectors.py
nodes.summary: Core warning detector functions that evaluate the current game state against configured thresholds and fire TTS warnings via the speech queue for resources, supply, and idle workers.

nodes.name: check_resources
nodes.summary: Checks minerals and gas levels against configured thresholds and triggers spoken warnings with cooldown gating, optionally recording to game history.

nodes.name: check_supply
nodes.summary: Evaluates supply gap against tiered thresholds and fires a spoken supply warning when capped or near-capped, respecting cooldown and recording to game history.

nodes.name: check_idle_workers
nodes.summary: Tracks idle worker onset time and fires a spoken warning after the configured idle_seconds duration, returning the onset timestamp for stateful tracking.

nodes.name: game_api.py
nodes.summary: Interfaces with the SC2 local API to detect game running state and captures the HUD via screen OCR, including a spike filter to suppress anomalous OCR readings between frames.

nodes.name: fetch_game_state
nodes.summary: Public entry point that checks whether SC2 is running and returns the current HUD state dict captured via OCR, or None if no game is in progress.

nodes.name: _capture_hud
nodes.summary: Captures all four HUD regions (minerals, gas, supply, idle workers) via screen OCR and assembles a state dict using configured screen capture coordinates.

nodes.name: _filter_spikes
nodes.summary: Applies a configurable anomaly filter that replaces values with the previous frame's value when the delta exceeds a per-key maximum, suppressing OCR noise spikes.

nodes.name: game_history.py
nodes.summary: GameHistoryManager class that tracks per-game warning counts in memory and persists them to SQLite via async DB calls, managing game lifecycle from start to end.

nodes.name: GameHistoryManager
nodes.summary: Stateful manager that tracks warning events across a single game session and synchronizes counts to the game_stats SQLite table on each warning and on game end.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the backend classes package, re-exporting SpeechQueue, CooldownTracker, and WakeWordDetector for convenient import by consumers.

nodes.name: cooldown_tracker.py
nodes.summary: Provides CooldownTracker, a lightweight per-key rate-limiter that tracks elapsed time to gate repeated warning emissions.

nodes.name: CooldownTracker
nodes.summary: Tracks per-key cooldown state using monotonic time, exposing ready() to check-and-reset and remaining() to query time left.

nodes.name: speech_queue.py
nodes.summary: Provides SpeechQueue, a thread-safe priority TTS daemon that serializes spoken warnings through macOS's say command.

nodes.name: SpeechQueue
nodes.summary: Priority queue backed by a daemon worker thread that invokes the macOS say command; accepts message, voice, and priority arguments.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a (priority, counter) tuple in PriorityQueue to maintain FIFO ordering within the same priority level.

nodes.name: voice_listener.py
nodes.summary: Provides VoiceListener, which captures a microphone phrase after a wake-word event, transcribes it via Google or Whisper STT, and parses it into structured VoiceCommand intents.

nodes.name: VoiceListener
nodes.summary: Listens for a spoken command after wake-word detection, transcribes with a configurable STT backend, and enqueues a VoiceCommand for the main loop to act on.

nodes.name: wake_word_detector.py
nodes.summary: Provides WakeWordDetector, which runs a background audio loop using openwakeword/ONNX to detect a configurable wake phrase and invoke a callback.

nodes.name: WakeWordDetector
nodes.summary: Daemon thread that streams 16 kHz audio chunks through an openwakeword ONNX model; fires on_wake callback when score exceeds sensitivity threshold, with refractory period to avoid double-triggers.
nodes.languageNotes: Drains remaining buffered audio after a wake event to prevent immediate re-trigger from residual audio in the stream buffer.

nodes.name: SQLiteConnector

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md establishes what SC2 Helper is and why it exists: a real-time coaching assistant that reads your StarCraft II HUD via screen OCR and speaks warnings aloud when you are floating resources, supply-capped, or leaving workers idle. Reading it first gives you the mental model and vocabulary you will need for every subsequent step in this tour.

tour.title: Architecture Overview
tour.description: The architecture document explains the two-process design that is the defining structural decision of this codebase: a customtkinter frontend process spawns the backend as a child subprocess. This separation keeps the UI responsive while the backend runs its tight OCR-polling loop independently. Understanding this boundary is essential before reading any code.

tour.title: UI Entry Point
tour.description: sc2_ui.py is the executable entry point for the entire application. It instantiates SC2HelperApp and calls mainloop(), which hands control to the customtkinter event loop. This single-file entry point follows the Python convention of keeping the launch bootstrapping minimal and delegating all real setup to the root window class.
tour.languageLesson: Python GUI applications use mainloop() to start the Tkinter event loop, which blocks until the window is closed. Keeping the entry point thin (just instantiate + mainloop) separates process startup from application logic.

tour.title: Runner Screen & Process Bridge
tour.description: RunnerScreen (runner_view.py) is the Start/Stop control panel shown to the user. When the user clicks Start, it delegates to RunnerController (runner_logic.py), which is the critical process bridge: it launches the backend as a subprocess using Python's subprocess module and pipes stdout back to the UI via callbacks. This is where the two-process architecture from Step 2 is actually implemented.
tour.languageLesson: Python's subprocess module can stream a child process's stdout line-by-line using iter(proc.stdout.readline, b''). Running this in a daemon thread prevents it from blocking the GUI's mainloop while still delivering live output to the UI.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: index.py is the backend process's entry point and its main polling loop. It orchestrates the entire game-monitoring cycle: it polls the SC2 local API to detect when a game is live, then continuously reads HUD values, runs the warning detectors, and manages voice command listening. With a fan-out of 3 it is the most connected node in the backend, importing detectors, game_history, and voice_listener — making it the hub that ties all backend subsystems together.

tour.title: HUD Data Pipeline
tour.description: Before warnings can fire, the application needs numbers from the screen. ocr.py captures the relevant screen regions using the mss library and feeds the screenshots to Tesseract OCR to extract integer values. game_api.py sits above ocr.py: it calls the SC2 local HTTP API to detect game state, invokes the OCR pipeline to read HUD values, and applies a spike filter to discard transient OCR noise before returning clean readings to the main loop.
tour.languageLesson: A spike filter discards readings that deviate dramatically from the previous value — for example, rejecting a parsed value of 9999 when the previous reading was 450. This guards against Tesseract misreading a single frame without requiring expensive multi-frame averaging.

tour.title: Shared Constants & HUD Layout
tour.description: constants.py and hud_elements.py define the vocabulary shared across the entire backend. constants.py holds the SC2 API base URL, TTS priority levels, and lookup maps for normalizing race and result strings. hud_elements.py defines HudElement dataclass instances for the four screen regions the application monitors — resources, supply, workers, and army — establishing the fixed coordinate system the OCR pipeline reads.

tour.title: Warning Detectors
tour.description: detectors.py contains the three core check functions — check_resources, check_supply, and check_idle_workers — that implement the domain logic of the assistant. Each function compares the latest OCR-extracted HUD values against configurable thresholds and, when a threshold is breached, dispatches a spoken warning through the speech queue. These are the functions that turn raw screen data into actionable coaching feedback.
tour.languageLesson: Separating the warning message content (messages.py) from the detection logic (detectors.py) makes it easy to add new message tones — strict, funny, or custom — without touching the threshold comparison code. get_message() acts as a strategy dispatcher selecting the right bank at runtime.

tour.title: Voice Output & Rate Limiting
tour.description: speech_queue.py implements a thread-safe priority queue that serializes all TTS output through macOS's say command. Because multiple detectors may trigger simultaneously, the queue ensures warnings are spoken one at a time in priority order and never overlap. cooldown_tracker.py adds a per-key rate limiter on top: once a warning fires for a given detector, that detector is silenced for a configurable cooldown window, preventing the same warning from repeating every poll cycle.
tour.languageLesson: A daemon thread (daemon=True) in Python terminates automatically when the main process exits, making it ideal for background workers like a TTS queue that should not keep the process alive after the user closes the application.

tour.title: Voice Control Pipeline
tour.description: SC2 Helper can also accept spoken commands from the user. wake_word_detector.py runs a background audio loop using OpenWakeWord and an ONNX model to listen for a configurable wake phrase without occupying the main thread. Once the wake phrase is detected, voice_listener.py captures the follow-up microphone audio, transcribes it via speech-to-text, and parses the transcript into a VoiceCommand intent that the main loop in index.py can act on.
tour.languageLesson: Wake-word detection using ONNX runs entirely on-device with no network round-trips, keeping latency low and avoiding the privacy concerns of cloud speech APIs. The two-stage pipeline (wake word then full transcription) saves resources by only activating the heavier STT model after the lightweight wake detector fires.

tour.title: Configuration & Service Layer
tour.description: service.py is the single authoritative interface for reading and writing application state: get_config, save_config, get_stats_history, and get_live_stats all wrap the async SQLite operations behind synchronous-friendly call sites. config_manager.py in the frontend is a thin re-export shim that lets UI code call these functions without directly importing from the backend package, preserving the process boundary established in Step 4.

tour.title: Data Layer
tour.description: The persistence layer consists of two files. db/__init__.py exposes get_db(), an async context manager that yields a database connection, hiding the aiosqlite implementation details from the rest of the backend. db/schema.py defines the CREATE TABLE statements for the config and game_stats tables and provides ensure_tables() which applies the schema on first run — acting as a lightweight migration system.
tour.languageLesson: An async context manager (async with get_db() as db) ensures the database connection is properly opened and closed even if an exception occurs mid-operation. Using aiosqlite allows the I/O-bound database calls to yield control back to the event loop rather than blocking it.

tour.title: Game History
tour.description: game_history.py provides GameHistoryManager, which accumulates per-game warning counts in memory while a match is in progress, then flushes the final tally to the game_stats SQLite table when the game ends. This bridges the real-time warning loop from Step 8 with the persistent data layer from Step 12, and feeds the game history dashboard in the UI.

tour.title: Settings UI
tour.description: SettingsScreen (settings_view.py) assembles four tabs into a single configuration panel: ConfigTab exposes every threshold, cooldown, supply-tier, voice, and OCR setting as a scrollable form; CoordsTab provides the countdown mouse-grab flow for capturing HUD screen coordinates. Together they give users full control over the parameters that drive the detectors, OCR pipeline, and voice system explored in previous steps.

tour.title: Tests & Dev Tooling
tour.description: test_detectors.py contains smoke tests that verify the three detector functions fire TTS warnings when thresholds are crossed and remain silent when cooldowns suppress them, giving fast regression coverage for the core domain logic. dev.py complements the tests with a hot-reload runner that watches src/ for file changes and automatically restarts the frontend, shortening the feedback loop during development.
